object_description: long hall-like volume of about 28 by 110 metres under a single uniform gabled roof
design_condition: the long hall volume takes its cue from the street- and river-parallel industrial halls, turning its main facade west towards the stream while the street side is closed and declared irrelevant for daily school life

positive: The volume is inspired by the street- and river-parallel industrial halls further east
The timber skeleton speaks a much more open and transparent language
The concise structure reads as an open spatial structure directly related to the outside space
This approach is visible at all levels of detail and works as a concept
The volumetric integration of the gymnasium gives a very generous usable area
The 110-metre promenade overlooking kindergarten, hall, sunken gymnasium and playrooms promises a tremendous density of interaction
This large space oriented both inwards and outwards is an interesting proposal
It testifies to an understanding of the school as a community spanning classes and ages
Placing the classrooms on the roof of the hall can create a radically contrasting, concentrated learning atmosphere
The wide top floor credibly implements the required division and flexibility
The very generous central zone and two roof terraces make a serious case for cross-classroom teaching
The load-bearing elements are timber with cores in recycled concrete
The foundation concept on strip foundations is not expected to significantly impair the groundwater flow
The ground floor develops along a lively open space facing the stream while the upper floors are quieter
The various uses are arranged sensibly and efficiently within the building
The variability and diversity of current and future forms of teaching under one roof is particularly appreciated
negative: The new alignment of the access road affects the scenic quality of the stream area
The open space quality along the street can only be compensated by the overall view of all outdoor areas
The street side is largely closed and declared irrelevant for daily school operation
The main facade facing west is taken to extremes at the cost of a rear facing the street
The absence of an underground garage and all parking along the street reflect this one-sidedness
Kindergarten and day structure are directly part of a lively, noisy sports and break operation, which is problematic
The required quiet and material rooms within the kindergarten are missing
Placing the classrooms and wet rooms on the roof of the hall is structurally challenging
Their remote arrangement risks spatial and operational distance from the school grounds and outdoor spaces
No information is provided on buoyancy problems
